Chapter 10: Living Out a God-Centered Marriage
So, you’ve reached the incredible milestone of marriage. But here’s the thing—marriage isn’t the finish line. It’s really just the start of a whole new adventure. A God-centered marriage is about continually growing, learning, and loving with intention. It’s a journey that asks for your heart and your effort, every single day.
There are a few gentle practices that can help keep your marriage healthy and rooted in faith. First, keep those lines of communication wide open. Even when life gets hectic, make it a point to talk, listen, and really share what’s going on inside.
Next, share your spiritual life. Pray together, dive into scripture side-by-side, and cheer each other on as you grow in faith. There’s something powerful about supporting each other’s spiritual journeys.
Don’t forget to serve each other in small, everyday ways. A little kindness, a thoughtful gesture, or a word of encouragement can mean the world. These simple acts build up trust and affection over time.
And stay connected to your community. Lean on mentors, friends, and your faith community for support and accountability. You don’t have to do this alone—having others around you makes the journey richer and more manageable.
Remember, marriage is a partnership, not a project. It’s about choosing—day after day—to love, to forgive, and to keep growing together. Some seasons will be full of joy, while others might bring challenges. But what really matters is that you’re walking the path together, with God right at the center.
In real life, this might look like setting aside time each week for a “marriage check-in.” Maybe you pray together before bed, or reach out for help when tough times come. It could also mean celebrating milestones, lifting up each other’s dreams, or finding ways to serve others as a team.
A God-centered marriage isn’t about being perfect. It’s about having a purpose. It’s built on the foundation of intentionality, faith, and love—the same foundation you started building during courtship. And with that, you keep growing, together, for a lifetime.
